items.t: In Grandview-Woodland, Vancouver, houses sold at a median of $1,900,000 across 63 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,565,000 and $2,225,000. The median house sat 7 days and sold for 99.4% of list.
Grandview-Woodland, Vancouver: 23 townhomes sold at a median of $1,085,000, with the middle half between $865,000 and $1,264,000. The median townhome took 8 days to sell and closed at 99.1% of list.

95 condos sold in Grandview-Woodland, Vancouver at a median of $664,900 (middle half $547,850 to $850,000). A typical condo in Grandview-Woodland, Vancouver spent 16 days on the market and closed at 98.6% of the asking price.

In Grandview-Woodland, Vancouver, duplexes sold at a median of $1,585,000 across 89 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,470,000 and $1,759,000. The median duplex sat 16 days and sold for 98.2% of list.

How Grandview-Woodland compares with the rest of Vancouver East

items.t: Houses in Grandview-Woodland have the 4th highest median of 15 Vancouver East sub-areas, $1,900,000. Collingwood is lowest at $1,510,000 and Fraser highest at $1,980,000. Killarney ($1,840,000) sits just below and Main ($1,905,500) sits just above.

Of 13 Vancouver East sub-areas with 5 or more townhome sales, Grandview-Woodland ranks 7th highest at $1,085,000; the range is $796,000 (Killarney) to $1,419,500 (Main). Renfrew VE ($1,044,400) sits just below and Knight ($1,100,000) sits just above.

Condos in Grandview-Woodland have the 6th highest median of 13 Vancouver East sub-areas, $664,900. Collingwood is lowest at $520,000 and Main highest at $898,950. Fraser ($647,000) sits just below and Knight ($673,000) sits just above.

Of 15 Vancouver East sub-areas with 5 or more duplex sales, Grandview-Woodland ranks 4th highest at $1,585,000; the range is $1,112,500 (Strathcona) to $1,919,000 (Main). Knight ($1,496,500) sits just below and Fraser ($1,685,000) sits just above.
